data.title: RBNZ Governor Sees Fuel Costs Potentially Feeding Broader Inflation
data.description: New Zealand’s central bank has seen some evidence that higher fuel costs may be feeding through into broader inflation, Governor Anna Breman said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: BTC Whale Withdraws Large Buy Order as Market Awaits Key Price Levels
data.description:
On November 18, a large BTC trader abruptly withdrew a sizable buy order in the afternoon. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, the Hyperliquid long quickly placed orders worth tens of millions of dollars at other price levels. Options implied volatility, concentrated profit-taking pressure overhead and funds waiting at lower levels are pushing BTC into a narrow trading range.

The Federal Reserve is scheduled to release minutes from its October meeting at 03:00 (UTC+8) tomorrow. At the previous meeting, some committee members voted in favor of a rate hike. After rebounding from a weekend low, Bitcoin saw U.S. spot ETFs return to net inflows for one day before flows turned negative again. Market participants are watching for key price levels as they await the minutes.

data.title: U.S. Holiday Spending Plans Top Last Year, With Growth Concentrated Among Wealthiest
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. consumers plan to spend more this holiday season than last year, but the increase is concentrated among the wealthiest households as many shoppers seek discounts and trim gift budgets.

A Conference Board survey found planned average spending on gifts and nongift items is up 5.9% from last year, or 3.2% after adjusting for inflation. Planned gift spending alone is up 2.3% after adjusting for prices. Only respondents with annual incomes of at least $200,000 plan to increase spending; their average gift budgets are 13.6% higher than in 2025. Expected gift spending is down among all other income groups.

Rising prices are squeezing many U.S. households' budgets for nonessential purchases. Larger-than-usual tax refunds and stock-market wealth effects supported consumer spending through much of this year, while wage growth largely failed to keep pace with inflation. About 38% of respondents plan to buy more promotional items, nearly 30% plan to buy fewer gifts, and 20% plan to switch to lower-priced brands or products.

The National Retail Federation reported similar findings last month, saying the top 10% of spenders will account for as much as 70% of total holiday sales as rising gasoline prices continue to pressure lower-income households.

data.title: AI | Firms Vie to Offer Anthropic Leveraged ETFs Before Stock Debut
data.description: According to Bloomberg, issuers are racing to position leveraged ETFs tied to Anthropic ahead of its stock debut, hoping their funds will attract the bulk of investor dollars. After SpaceX’s public debut, several leveraged ETFs tied to the company launched, but only one attracted meaningful assets. That outcome has raised the stakes for Anthropic fund issuers.

data.description: According to Jin10, Len Blavatnik, a major shareholder of Warner Music (WMG.O), increased his holdings of SpaceX (SPCX.O) shares to a value of about $5 billion.

data.title: STOCKS | Hedge Funds Add Alibaba and Futu as Stanley Druckenmiller’s Family Office Exits Baidu
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Bloomberg, 1,191 hedge funds’ third-quarter 13F filings showed net additions of 5.5 million Alibaba ADRs, reversing two consecutive quarters of net selling. Funds also added 2.08 million Futu shares, after reducing their holdings in the previous quarter.

They cut Baidu holdings by 3.84 million shares after adding 3.5 million in the second quarter. Appaloosa LP, run by David Tepper, reduced its Baidu position, which it had increased in the prior quarter. Duquesne Family Office LLC, Stanley Druckenmiller’s family office, exited its Baidu position, opened in the previous quarter.

Other large additions included 12.06 million shares of Kanzhun, 11.68 million of JD.com and 2.54 million of PDD Holdings. Hedge funds continued adding pharmaceutical stocks, including Zai Lab and BeiGene, while reducing holdings in electric-vehicle makers such as Nio and XPeng. They also continued trimming the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (KWEB).

data.title: AI | US Acts to Restrict China's Access to Nvidia Chips
data.description:
The US is moving to curb China's access to Nvidia chips, Bloomberg reported. Mary Lovely, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, said she would set a “low bar” for a meeting among US President Donald Trump, Xi and Putin and does not expect much to come out of the summit. She called that “unfortunate” given the topics the leaders need to discuss.

Lovely said the US should “proceed very carefully” on its stance toward limiting chip exports to China as the race for AI dominance continues.

data.title: AI | Faster Cyber-Flaw Fixes Are Worsening Outages at Firms
data.description: AI is pushing firms to fix cyber flaws faster, worsening outages. US officials said recent disruptions were not caused by cyberattacks, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Microsoft Says Copilot Undercuts Anthropic and OpenAI on Operating Cost
data.description: Microsoft says customers are choosing its Copilot AI assistant over Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT because Copilot is cheaper to operate, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Fed Minutes: Vast Majority of Officials See Upside Inflation Risks
data.description: According to Jin10, minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting showed that most FOMC members expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term before gradually declining to 2% over time. However, amid high energy prices and continued constraints on refined-fuel supplies, a “vast majority” of officials saw upside risks to the inflation outlook. Many officials also viewed AI infrastructure development as an important source of inflation risk. Most said costs driven by AI construction and related investment could broadly pass through to consumer-goods and business-services prices and persist for an extended period.

data.title: Colombia Cites $43 Billion Investment Commitments Amid Fiscal Strain
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Colombia secured $43.2 billion in investment and financing commitments during a three-day effort to attract foreign capital in New York, more than double the government’s initial target.

data.title: Sen. Capito Says FAA Funding Needs More Accountability and Transparency
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Republican Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia said FAA funding needs greater accountability and transparency. She said Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's request for $50 billion in additional funding did not meet that standard, while adding that the transportation system needs funding backed on a bipartisan basis. Capito also discussed energy permitting reform and concerns about advanced chips going to China.

data.title: Aclara Resources CEO Says Brazil Needs More Mining Incentives as Firm Considers Plant
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Aclara Resources’ chief executive said Brazil needs to offer miners more incentives as the company weighs a future rare-earth separation plant in the country.

data.title: Fed Minutes: Some Participants Leaned Toward a 25-Basis-Point October Hike, Citing High Inflation and Little Evidence of Cooling
data.description: According to Jin10, the Fed minutes said some participants leaned toward a 25-basis-point rate hike at the October meeting, stressing that inflation was too high and that there was little evidence it was easing.
